_comment: THE catalogue of navigable sections — the sidebar's contents, the routes they
reach, and the API prefixes each one legitimately calls. One file, vendored
byte-identically into every service's src/lib and into web/src/lib, because a
service's Docker build context is its own directory (see scripts/check-shared.sh,
which fails the build if any copy drifts).
JSON, not JS, for exactly one reason: the services are CommonJS and the web is
an ES module Vite build. A .js file cannot be required by one and imported by
the other without a wrapper per side, and a wrapper per side is a second place
for the list to drift. Both `require()` and Vite read JSON natively.
WHAT EACH FIELD IS FOR
key         stable id. Stored in the Sidebar Visibility config and matched by
the server guard, so it must never be renamed casually — a rename
silently un-hides whatever an admin had hidden.
to/label/   presentation, read only by web/src/components/Layout.jsx. Moved
icon/end/   here verbatim from that file's old NAV_SECTIONS constant.
matchPaths/
nonAdminLabel
roles       THE BASELINE: who may ever reach this section. Absent = every
signed-in role. The visibility config can only ever SUBTRACT from
this, never add — so a mis-ticked checkbox cannot hand a
housekeeper the folio ledger.
core        cannot be hidden from anyone. Dashboard is where a blocked route
redirects to, and Settings is where the person changing their own
password goes; hiding either strands the user.
api         the API prefixes this page actually calls, measured from the page
source rather than guessed. See navScope.js for how these combine
— a prefix stays reachable while ANY section that lists it is
still visible to the user, which is what stops hiding Folios from
also breaking the folio tab of Arrivals.
_alwaysAllowComment: Prefixes no section owns and no configuration may ever close: signing in,
reading your own account, changing your own password, signing out, and the
public guest-facing endpoints that have no session at all. Locking someone out
of /api/auth would make the misconfiguration unrecoverable from the browser.
_configurableRolesComment: Roles an admin may configure. ADMIN is deliberately absent and the write route
rejects it: an admin who hid Settings and Users from ADMIN would have removed
the only screen that could put them back, from the only role that can reach it.

items.label: Dashboard
_apiComment: The operational day-sheets, plus ONE report sub-path. Every role
legitimately needs these here — housekeeping reads arrivals and
in-house through OPS_READ and has no other section that would grant
them, so dropping any would break the dashboard for the role least
able to work around it.
/api/reports/room-status, not /api/reports: the room-status donut is
ALL_STAFF and is the one call on this page with no .catch() of its
own, so denying it takes the whole dashboard down with it. Claiming
the WHOLE /api/reports prefix here would be the easy fix and the
wrong one — dashboard is a core section, so anything it claims is
pinned open for every role forever, and hiding Reports & Revenue
from a manager is meant to close the revenue endpoints too, not just
the sidebar link. Prefixes match on segment boundaries, so naming the
exact sub-path costs nothing and gives up nothing.
/api/audit is deliberately absent for the same reason; that call
already degrades to an empty list on this page.

items.label: Messages
_rolesComment: No `roles` key, so every signed-in role — which is the whole point.
Messages are addressed to a person, not to a department: restricting
this by role would be deciding which staff may be contacted, and a
housekeeper who cannot reply to the manager is not a chat feature.
Not `core` though: an admin may still hide it per role from Sidebar
Visibility if they do not want a given role messaging at all. Core is
for the two pages that strand a user when hidden (Dashboard, Settings),
and this is not one of them.
_chromeComment: RENDERED IN THE TOPBAR, NOT THE SIDEBAR. `chrome` moves where the
entry is DRAWN and changes nothing else: the row still scopes its
API prefixes, still respects `roles`, and an admin can still hide it
per role from Sidebar Visibility (which then hides the topbar
control too). Layout.jsx skips chrome:'topbar' entries when it
builds the rail and renders this one beside the notification bell.
Deleting the entry instead would have been wrong twice over: it
prefixes alone), and it would drop this row's /api/users claim —
which is the only thing keeping the contact list working for a role
that has the Users section hidden. See _apiComment below.
_apiComment: /api/users is listed because the contact list reads
/api/users/directory, which is authenticated-only rather than
STAFF_ROLES-gated (see services/auth/src/routes/users.routes.js).
This widens nothing: prefixes here are a union that keeps a path open
while a visible section needs it, and the requireRole guards on the
other /api/users routes are untouched — an auditor calling GET
/api/users still gets Forbidden. What it buys is that hiding
Housekeeping from the front desk (the other section claiming
/api/users) no longer takes their contact list down with it.

items.label: Amenities & Facilities
_mergeComment: /api/promo-codes lives here, not under 'rooms': the feature moved
to the Amenities page's Promo Codes tab (canManagePromos in
Amenities.jsx). Left in 'rooms' too, this prefix would silently
break for MANAGER the moment an admin hides Hotel Rooms — a real
page they no longer touch has nothing to do with a commercial
promo they still manage from Amenities.

items.label: Reports & Revenue
_mergeComment: Night Audit used to be its own top-level item here (key 'audit',
icon 'sunrise'). It is now a sibling page reached through the
the same pattern /revenue already used — one rail entry, several
routes behind it. /audit is a matchPath for exactly that reason:
it keeps this rail row highlighted while standing on the Night
Audit page, same as /revenue already did.
The 'audit' key is gone from the catalogue, so BOTH copies that
keyed off it had to move: App.jsx's ProtectedRoute for /audit now
checks section="reports", and the audit tour step in
TutorialTour.jsx now gates on hasSection('reports') instead of a
key that no longer exists (which would have made hasSection()
return false forever and silently drop the step).

items.label: Activity Log
_rolesComment: ADMIN only, and narrower than the Night Audit page on purpose. This
is the record of what every member of staff did, MANAGER included —
a manager who can review (and be seen reviewing) their own
department's actions is a separation-of-duties problem, not a
convenience. Same reasoning as Service Health above, which withholds
operational data from MANAGER for the same reason.
ADMIN is absent from configurableRoles, so this cannot be hidden from
the only role that can reach it.
